tweets.text:
When I was 14 my dad made me work as a waiter at his place

I got paid and was excited but I hated this job so much that I had an idea

An idea that I’d learn to code NOW and by 17-18 I’d find a well paid remote job

Starting with Python and at 17 moving to JavaScript it led to roughly 9000+ rejected applications (obviously duhh)

That first failure led to creating an agency where I made my first online $

Agency died in a year and a half and 2 failed startups led to @mediafa_st where I decided to help people with Reddit marketing without getting suspended

14 months and it made over $40,000 completely changing my life 

In those 14 months I met so many incredible people, built my X audience to 7k followers and learned a shit load of new stuff - building, coding, marketing, closing deals

4 months ago I launched startup number 4 and last month it made over $6,500, making my May income over $10k

Now I pivot MediaFast to GEO - better offer, better landing, goal to scale to $10k/month 

This is an incredibly long journey. It sucked in moments. It was fun. I celebrated every victory. And I was afraid on every fall

Your main goal is to adapt. Learn. Fail, adapt and try again!

The other side is worth it 🎯

tweets.text:
Yesterday I got my first hater

A guy asked for a refund in MediaFast chat

I pointed him to our refund policy, which clearly states we don’t offer refunds

He messaged again, same request
I redirected him once more and shared the rules publicly (we have a Discord-like rules channel)

Then he blew up.
He posted on X calling me a scammer and commented the same thing under two of my posts.

Turns out:
- His DM was sitting in my spam folder
- After a 2-minute conversation, I realized he never even used the app
- He wanted a Reddit scheduler (a side feature), decided it “made no sense” for him and jumped to conclusions

I explained that MediaFast’s real goal is different: 
It finds subreddits, tells you what to post, when to post, how to post, and helps you market on Reddit without getting suspended

I told him to be careful before calling someone a scammer based on his own mistake, wished him well, and moved on

Later, he deleted all his posts and comments

Not angry

Just a reminder that shipping publicly also means dealing with stuff like this
